items.description: after the expand migration runs, a stock row seeded with inventory_code 'A12-B7-S001' (per-run-unique sku via uuid.uuid4()) has batch_number='B7' and serial_number='S001'

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), a single-step alembic downgrade -1 removes only batch_number and serial_number from stock_records and leaves all other columns intact; a subsequent re-upgrade re-adds both columns — confirming the additive round-trip schema shape is correct (PI1-expand-migration-reversible)

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), rows seeded before the downgrade (including nonconforming rows whose batch_number and serial_number would be NULL) survive the single-step downgrade with all pre-existing columns (id, sku, location, quantity, inventory_code) intact and no row dropped; after re-upgrade the added columns reappear

verified directly against the real branch database: after the expand migration commits, every pre-existing stock_records row is present (none dropped), batch_number and serial_number columns exist, and all conforming rows have been backfilled — confirming the add-columns-and-backfill executed atomically as a single committed transaction with no partial state (PI2-expand-migration-atomic)

after the F6 expand migration is applied to the real branch database, an attempt to INSERT a stock_records row with a negative quantity is rejected by the database with a CHECK constraint violation, confirming CHECK(quantity >= 0) was not weakened by the migration
after the expand migration runs, a stock row seeded with a two-segment inventory_code 'X-1' (per-run-unique sku via uuid.uuid4()) has batch_number=NULL and serial_number=NULL
after the expand migration runs, a stock row seeded with a bare single-segment inventory_code 'c' (per-run-unique sku via uuid.uuid4()) has batch_number=NULL and serial_number=NULL

after the expand migration runs, the nonconforming row seeded with inventory_code 'X-1' (per-run-unique sku) still exists in stock_records with all original column values intact (no row dropped or corrupted)

after the F6 expand migration is applied, the delta row count for the test's own seeded stock_records rows is identical to the pre-migration count (no seeded row dropped or corrupted), verified directly against the real branch database

when the integrity probe is called over a post-migration table containing one conforming and two nonconforming rows (seeded with per-run-unique skus via uuid.uuid4()), it returns a nonconforming count delta of exactly 2

after the expand migration runs, a stock row whose inventory_code leading segment differs from its pre-seeded canonical location column still has the original location value unchanged (per-run-unique sku via uuid.uuid4())

after the F6 expand migration and backfill are applied to the real branch database, an attempt to INSERT a stock_records row with a (sku, location) pair that duplicates an existing row is rejected with a unique-constraint violation, confirming UNIQUE(sku, location) was not weakened by adding batch_number and serial_number

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), after applying the S2 contract up migration, a schema diff confirms the stock_records table has no inventory_code column while batch_number and serial_number are present

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), rows seeded before the S2 contract up migration (including rows with NULL batch_number/serial_number, using per-run-unique skus via uuid.uuid4()) are all present after inventory_code is dropped, with location, batch_number, and serial_number values unchanged and no row dropped or corrupted

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), a single-step alembic downgrade -1 from the S2 contract migration reconstructs inventory_code as a text column recomposed from location + batch_number + serial_number joined with the '-' delimiter, and the canonical location column is unchanged

on an isolated ephemeral migration branch (@pytest.mark.migration), after the down migration reconstructs inventory_code, re-applying the S2 up migration drops inventory_code again, leaving batch_number and serial_number present and every pre-existing row intact with location unchanged — confirming the complete reversibility round-trip
